items.title: America Becomes a Playable Strategy Game
points: Andrej Karpathy used Claude (an AI chatbot/coding assistant made by Anthropic) to transform the US into an interactive strategy game map with 45,000 lines of code, written in 7 hours, pulling from 31 public data sources.

Each city's wealth reflects actual income, workforce represents real population, and specializations are determined by genuine employment percentages (e.g., 1 in 4 California tech workers vs. 1 in 14 nationwide).
Users can toggle views between income levels, historical disasters, and national landmarks shown as in-game wonders, plus click any county to see comparative charts against other regions.
Released as a playable prototype, with hopes others will develop it into a full strategy game.

items.title: AI Helps Hobbyists Hunt for Exoplanets
points: An OpenAI employee and an email startup founder used AI to scan space telescope data for exoplanet signatures (tiny dips in starlight when a planet passes in front of its star).
OpenAI's Codex tool found 200+ signals across 100,000 stars; the startup founder's larger search found 49 potential planets across 19 million stars, still ongoing.
Ten of the OpenAI researcher's signals matched known planets, validating the method; one candidate orbits a star half our sun's size every 13.8 days and is 2.4 times Earth's width.
An independent SETI Institute astronomer confirmed two of the same signals; at least one candidate is now with the space telescope research team for formal verification.

items.title: Neuralink Hits Major Regulatory Milestone
points: FDA approved Neuralink's first formal clinical trial for brain implants in severely paralyzed ALS patients across multiple hospitals, a critical step toward medical device approval.
30+ people already use Neuralink implants successfully, logging thousands of cumulative hours for texting, computer control, and communication without touching devices.

The trial will measure how much the implant enables independent activity and monitor long-term safety, moving brain-computer interfaces (devices that let the brain directly control computers or machines) from lab research to standard medical evaluation.
Some current users have returned to school and resumed personal relationships through device-enabled communication.

items.title: Pocket-Sized AI Runs Offline Models Locally
points: Tiiny AI Pocket is a power-bank-sized device that runs full-scale open-source AI models (publicly available AI software anyone can download and modify) directly on Mac or PC without internet connection.
All files stay encrypted locally with no cloud uploads, monthly subscriptions, or usage tracking.
Designed to run large models—similar to those normally requiring data center resources—on consumer hardware, easing privacy concerns for sensitive documents.
One-time device purchase covers cost, with no recurring subscription fees.

items.title: Five New AI Tools Launched This Week
points: Elementor's Agent Ready Scanner audits websites for AI accessibility.
Meshy converts photos into 3D models.
Sidelong saves and lets users query personal content.
Kinetik generates social media content.
MailSweeper cleans up Gmail inboxes.
